create_ignore_already_exists.description: If set to true, skip repository creation if a repository with the same name already exists.
create_ignore_already_exists.rationale: Toggles idempotent creation so applying against an already-existing repository succeeds instead of erroring. This is a Terraform/automation convenience flag with no bearing on access control, encryption, or auditing, so it is not a useful platform-security policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

name.description:
Resource name of the repository, of the form '{{repo}}'.
The repo name may contain slashes. eg, 'name/with/slash'
name.rationale: name is not a security_impact as it is required to identify the resource and does not directly impact the security of the resource.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: project is not a security_impact as it is used to identify the project in which the resource exists. If it is not provided, the provider project will be used.

pubsub_configs.description:
How this repository publishes a change in the repository through Cloud Pub/Sub.
Keyed by the topic names.

pubsub_configs.message_format.description:
The format of the Cloud Pub/Sub messages.
- PROTOBUF: The message payload is a serialized protocol buffer of SourceRepoEvent.
- JSON: The message payload is a JSON string of SourceRepoEvent. Possible values: ["PROTOBUF", "JSON"]
pubsub_configs.message_format.rationale: Selects the wire encoding (JSON vs PROTOBUF) of the Pub/Sub notifications emitted on repository changes. The encoding is a downstream-integration preference and does not enable, disable, or route auditing itself, so constraining it does not improve security.

pubsub_configs.service_account_email.description:
Email address of the service account used for publishing Cloud Pub/Sub messages.
This service account needs to be in the same project as the PubsubConfig. When added,
the caller needs to have iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission on this service account.
If unspecified, it defaults to the compute engine default service account.
pubsub_configs.service_account_email.rationale: service_account_email is a security_impact as it specifies the service account used for publishing Cloud Pub/Sub messages. Using a dedicated service account with the principle of least privilege can help to minimize the potential attack surface and reduce the risk of unauthorized access or actions within the repository.

pubsub_configs.topic.description: The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
pubsub_configs.topic.rationale: topic is not a security_impact as it is required to specify the Cloud Pub/Sub topic to which the repository will publish changes. It does not directly impact the security of the resource, but rather defines the communication channel for repository events.
